title: Israeli strikes kill nine in Gaza, Israeli minister says no deal to halt attacks
gist: Israeli airstrikes killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza on Aug. 2, 2026 despite Trump's claim of a breakthrough on implementing last year's ceasefire, with Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen saying no deal exists to halt attacks and urging Israel — which already controls 70% of the Strip — to take full control. The 15-point roadmap published by Trump's Board of Peace is stuck on sequencing: Hamas will only store weapons after Israeli withdrawal, while Israel will not withdraw without genuine disarmament first.

themes.theme: Ceasefire breakthrough contradicted on the ground

insights.claim: Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza for a second straight day on Aug. 2, 2026, killing at least nine Palestinians across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah, Khan Younis and Jabalia, despite Trump's announced breakthrough on implementing the Gaza ceasefire.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Announced diplomatic breakthroughs in this conflict are not tracking operational reality — discount ceasefire headlines against strike tempo.
insights.quote: Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza for a second straight day on Sunday, killing at least nine Palestinians, despite U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough

insights.claim: At least 1,230 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli strikes since the ceasefire was reached in October 2025.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A four-figure post-ceasefire death toll quantifies how little the existing agreement constrains military action, setting the baseline for any new roadmap.
insights.quote: At least 1,230 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli strikes since a ceasefire was reached in October.
insights.locator: At least 1,230 Palestinians have been killed

insights.claim: The Israeli military said the Deir al-Balah strikes targeted two commanders of Hamas' elite 'Nukhba' force, while the Gaza City and Jabalia strikes targeted 'military operatives' still under review.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Israel is framing continued operations as targeted decapitation, which gives it a rationale to keep striking under any implemented ceasefire.
insights.locator: The Israeli military said the strikes in Deir al-Balah

insights.claim: Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen, a member of Netanyahu's security cabinet, said there is no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that Israel — which already controls 70% of the Strip — should take full control of it.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A security cabinet member publicly advocating full occupation signals the Israeli policy floor is territorial control, not ceasefire implementation.
insights.quote: there was no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already controls 70% of the Strip, to take full control of it
insights.locator: Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen said on Sunday

insights.claim: Cohen told Army Radio he does not believe Hamas will disarm and expects it to play games and hide its weaponry instead.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Senior Israeli officials are pre-emptively delegitimizing the disarmament step, which is the roadmap's linchpin — low odds of implementation.
insights.locator: Cohen told Army Radio he did not believe Hamas would disarm

insights.claim: Netanyahu has not publicly commented on the US-backed initiative, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called it unacceptable and said Israel should continue assassinating Hamas leaders.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Netanyahu's silence plus open coalition opposition indicates the Israeli government has not bought into the US plan, a key constraint on Washington's leverage.
insights.locator: Netanyahu has not commented publicly on the initiative

insights.claim: Trump's Board of Peace, the US-led body overseeing the Gaza ceasefire, published a 15-point roadmap on Friday setting out the final implementation steps, which has yet to be implemented.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A formal, published US framework exists — its implementation milestones become the checkpoints for judging regional de-escalation.
insights.locator: Trump's Board of Peace, the U.S.-led body overseeing the ceasefire

insights.claim: The roadmap is deadlocked on sequencing: Hamas says it will hand over weapons for storage only after Israel halts operations and withdraws, while an Israeli official says there will be no withdrawal from current positions unless Hamas undergoes 'genuine disarmament'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The mutual first-move problem is the binding constraint; without a third-party guarantor to break it, expect continued attrition rather than implementation.
insights.quote: An Israeli official told Reuters there would be no withdrawal from the military's current positions unless Hamas undergoes "genuine disarmament".

insights.claim: Trump said on Thursday that a breakthrough had occurred after Hamas agreed to disarm under a US-backed initiative to implement the ceasefire agreement reached last year in Egypt.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Hamas' conditional acceptance was the basis for the breakthrough claim, so the announcement rests on a concession Israel disputes is real.
insights.locator: Trump said on Thursday there had been a breakthrough

insights.claim: UAE-based former senior Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan said in a Facebook post that Jared Kushner told him he was working with the Israeli side to stop attacks on Gaza, and that the agreement's success now depends on Israel fully ending its daily attacks.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Signals a back-channel involving Gulf-based Palestinian figures, but the sourcing is a social media post the State Department has not confirmed.
insights.locator: Former senior Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan
